summary: The study presents an Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) process for growing p-type tin(II) monoxide (SnO) thin films using the precursors Sn(dmamp)2 and H2O. The process is conducted at low temperatures (90–210 °C) and results in single-phase SnO films with p-type conductivity, high transparency, and good conformality. The ALD process was confirmed to produce SnO films with a wide optical band gap and suitable electrical properties for electronic applications.
evidence: The SnO ALD process was conducted at low temperatures ranging between 90 and 210 °C, which is compatible with conventional organic and flexible substrates. The study also reports that the SnO films showed p-type conductivity with carrier concentrations of 3.4 × 10^17 to 1.6 × 10^18 cm−3 and Hall mobility values of 0.4 −2.9 cm2/(V·s).
